original_title: Breaking Benjamin frontman pauses concert to rant about Fallout 4 modding beef: 'There was a modder in the community that was really mean to me'
summary_en: Rock frontman Benjamin Burnley took a break from performing to passionately advocate for his own Fallout 4 mod, urging fans to boost its download numbers and retaliate against a perceived online bully.
ai_analysis: This unexpected concert interlude highlights the deep passion and sometimes volatile nature of online modding communities, even extending to well-known musicians.

en.title: Breaking Benjamin Frontman Rants About Fallout 4 Modding Beef On Stage
en.summary: Rock frontman Benjamin Burnley took a break from performing to passionately advocate for his own Fallout 4 mod, urging fans to boost its download numbers and retaliate against a perceived online bully.
en.body:
While most bands stick to music during their sets, **Breaking Benjamin** frontman **Benjamin Burnley** decided to use a recent concert in Holmdel, NJ, as a pulpit for a very specific, and rather passionate, plea to his audience: download his **Fallout 4** mod. The rock star dedicated a significant portion of his performance time to discuss a dispute he's having with another modder in the **Fallout 4** community, whom he claims has been bullying him.

Burnley's on-stage rant, captured by concertgoers and shared online, lasted over four minutes. He implored attendees, even those who don't play the game, to head to Nexus Mods and download his creation, titled 'True First Person.' The motivation? To spite a fellow modder who Burnley alleges was overly critical of his work. "There was a modder in the community that was really mean to me and bullying me, saying, 'Oh, your mod is shit. You don't know what you're fucking doing,'" Burnley stated during the concert. He then vowed to "blow his fucking downloads out of the water" by promoting his own mod relentlessly. The band's stage crew even displayed the mod's details on the venue's screens, adding a visual element to the unusual performance segment.

## A Musician's Modding Crusade

This isn't the first time **Breaking Benjamin**, or **Benjamin Burnley** specifically, has made headlines for veering into gaming-related topics during live shows. Past incidents include passionate, and at times lengthy, rants about **Star Wars Battlefront** and discussions about **Transformers**. This ongoing engagement with gaming culture suggests a genuine passion from the frontman that extends beyond his musical career. The 'True First Person' mod itself aims to enhance the immersion in **Fallout 4** by rendering the player character's full body in first-person view, a notable departure from the game's default floating arms. Burnley emphasized that modding should be about growth and learning, expressing frustration with what he perceived as immediate, harsh criticism from another creator. The mod was indeed updated shortly after the concert, indicating Burnley's commitment to its development.

## Community's Reaction and What's Next

The audience reaction to Burnley's extended monologue was mixed. While some fans seemed to enjoy the unique spectacle, others were heard calling for the band to play music. Online, discussions about the incident have sparked debate, with some finding it relatable and others questioning the appropriateness of using a concert stage for a personal modding dispute. Regardless, the event has certainly put Burnley's 'True First Person' mod on the map for a wider audience. As **Breaking Benjamin** continues their tour, it remains to be seen if such gaming-centric intermissions will become a regular feature of their shows. Fans eager to support Burnley's endeavor can find the 'True First Person' mod on Nexus Mods, with updates expected to continue.

content_raw: Local Man Benjamin Burnley interrupts a Breaking Benjamin concert with a rant about his True First Person 1.2 Fallout 4 mod from An amazing scene played out over the weekend at a Breaking Benjamin concert in Holmdel, NJ, as captured by Reddit user im_all_ears (embedded above). Band frontman Benjamin Burnley spent over four minutes imploring the audience to download his Fallout 4 mod in an effort to stick it to another modder who Burnley says bullied him over the quality of his work. "There was a modder in the community that was really mean to me and bullying me, saying, 'Oh, your mod is shit. You don't know what you're fucking doing,'" said Burnley. "So I'm doing this every fucking night, and blowing his fucking downloads out of the water." That was a mere two minutes into the four-and-a-half minute rant. Someone behind the scenes at the venue even joined in, putting the mod's details up on screens. "Even if you fuckin' don't play that game, go and download it. It's on Nexus Mods," said Burnley. "Tomorrow I better see all my motherfuckin' downloads going up." One attendee shouted: "Play some music!" Others in the crowd were loving it. Burnley kept going, telling the audience to wait for his new update to drop before downloading the mod. "When you post a mod, you're supposed to be able to grow and learn and make it better," Burnley said. "And right off the bat, this fucking asshole was shitting on my mod." Sure enough, the mod, which is called 'True First Person,' was last updated on Sunday. Here's how Burnely describes the mod on its Nexus Mods page : "Fallout 4's vanilla first person shows a pair of floating arms. This mod replaces that with a True First Person perspective where your player character's full body is rendered and visible in first person. Look down and you'll see your body, legs, clothing and equipped gear as part of the same character you see in third person. Your perspective also stays in first person during interactions that would normally force the camera out, such as workstations, power armor, etc." The mod is tagged "AI assisted," so presumably an amount of vibe coding went into it. The comments are now full of fans reacting to the concert, so actual assessments of how well it works are hard to come by, but Burnley has posted a video of the mod in action . "Brother I'm at your concert right now. You have my download," reads one post on the mod's page. Burnley, whose Nexus Mods username is "killemloud," thanked the poster that same night, after the show. Breaking Benjamin was formed in 1999, and has a previous connection to gaming: the single "Blow Me Away," which it recorded for the Halo 2 soundtrack.
